source: AI Engineering Field Manual — 2026 edition (50 pages, 13 stages, 48-week first pass)

stages.title: PYTHON + C++
stages.subtitle: Two languages; one engineering standard

concepts.title: CPU + MEMORY
concepts.detail: Stack vs heap, process address space, pointers/references, value vs identity, cache locality.

concepts.title: MODERN C++
concepts.detail: RAII, vectors, spans, ownership, move semantics, templates, const, exceptions.

concepts.title: PYTHON CORE
concepts.detail: Functions, iterators, exceptions, context managers, packaging, OOP and protocols.

concepts.title: TYPES
concepts.detail: C++ compile-time checks; Python annotations plus mypy strict and runtime schema checks.

concepts.title: ASYNC I/O
concepts.detail: Event loop, await suspension, cancellation, timeouts and bounded concurrency.

concepts.title: COMPLEXITY
concepts.detail: Big-O is a bound; benchmark actual allocations, data sizes and hot paths.

concepts.title: DEBUGGING
concepts.detail: GDB/lldb, sanitizers, tracemalloc, cProfile, tracebacks and logging context.

concepts.title: TESTING
concepts.detail: pytest, hypothesis, GoogleTest/Catch2; deterministic fixtures and failure cases.

stages.readiness: Build an identical top-k scoring library in C++20 and typed Python, then compare behavior, memory and runtime on realistic vectors.

lab.summary: Build an identical top-k scoring library in C++20 and typed Python, then compare behavior, memory and runtime on realistic vectors.
milestones: Define the same input contract in both languages: scores are finite floats, k is nonnegative, and ties are stable by original index.
Implement a reference Python sort and a C++ partial_sort/heap candidate. Record exact semantics of NaN rejection and empty arrays.
Expose a CLI accepting JSON and returning typed JSON; test error exit codes, malformed payloads and unicode file paths.
Benchmark for n=100, 10k, 1M and k=5/100. Measure allocations, wall time and p95 over repeated runs.

failures.title: Overflow / nonfinite
failures.detail: NaN, infinity, oversized k, floating tie cases.

failures.title: Ownership bugs
failures.detail: Dangling view or mutable shared state in C++.

failures.title: Benchmark fraud
failures.detail: Compare algorithms with unequal semantics or include cold startup in one run.

failures.title: Async misuse
failures.detail: CPU-bound loops blocking Python event loop; use process/native worker.

evidence: For any finite input, outputs are unique in-range indices, and len(out)=min(k,n).
Compare C++ and Python outputs over 10k seeded random cases including ties and extremes.
ASan/UBSan clean; mypy --strict and ruff pass; benchmark warm-up documented.
adversarial: Which data copies dominate peak RSS?
Why not use C++ for every service?
Which semantics must cross language boundaries?

stages.title: CS + DEV ENGINEERING
stages.subtitle: Algorithms, OS, networks and reproducible delivery

concepts.title: DATA STRUCTURES
concepts.detail: Arrays, maps, trees, heaps, bloom filters, priority queues; know complexity and memory shape.

concepts.title: OPERATING SYSTEMS
concepts.detail: Processes, threads, file descriptors, memory mapping, signals and scheduling.

concepts.title: NETWORKING
concepts.detail: DNS, TCP/TLS, HTTP/2, status codes, retries, idempotency and timeouts.

concepts.title: GIT
concepts.detail: Small commits, bisect, rebasing, branch protection, reviewable diffs and release tags.

concepts.title: CONTAINERS
concepts.detail: Images vs runtime, layer caching, build reproducibility, non-root users and health probes.

concepts.title: CONCURRENCY
concepts.detail: Threads vs processes vs coroutines; queues, backpressure, race conditions and locks.

concepts.title: CI/CD
concepts.detail: Format, lint, type-check, tests, SCA scan, container build and deployment gates.

concepts.title: OBSERVABILITY
concepts.detail: Structured logs, trace IDs, basic metrics and measured service-level objectives.

stages.readiness: Create a small job execution service that accepts tasks, runs bounded workers and survives kill/restart without duplicate side effects.

lab.summary: Create a small job execution service that accepts tasks, runs bounded workers and survives kill/restart without duplicate side effects.
milestones: Use PostgreSQL job rows with unique idempotency keys and an explicit pending/running/succeeded/failed state machine.
Implement lease expiry and compare-and-swap job claiming in a transaction; worker termination must not lose work.
Write a multi-stage Dockerfile; scan dependencies and drop root privileges before deployment.
Exercise 100 concurrent submissions, random SIGKILL and DB outages. Document lost, duplicate and delayed work separately.

failures.title: Poison task
failures.detail: Repeatedly failing input blocks queue without DLQ policy.

failures.title: Partition
failures.detail: DB unreachable; bounded retry instead of unbounded loops.

failures.title: Double execution
failures.detail: Lease expiry while old worker is still running.

failures.title: Resource growth
failures.detail: Orphan subprocesses, file handles or unbounded logs.

evidence: Prove concurrency safety with at least 20 competing workers.
Inject SIGKILL after side effect but before acknowledgement; handle retries idempotently.
Demonstrate p95 time-to-start and steady-state queue depth under load.
adversarial: Explain your delivery guarantee: at-most, at-least or effectively once.
What protects side effects after a worker timeout?
How are secrets handled across CI and runtime?

stages.title: FULL-STACK + DATA
stages.subtitle: Frontend, backend, SQL, cache and secure contracts

concepts.title: WEB FUNDAMENTALS
concepts.detail: DOM, forms, accessibility, browser storage, HTTP, CORS and rendering behavior.

concepts.title: TYPESCRIPT
concepts.detail: Discriminated unions, strict mode, async fetch, schema validation and typed API clients.

concepts.title: REACT
concepts.detail: Component state, effects, mutations, loading/error UI, memoization only when measured.

concepts.title: HTTP APIS
concepts.detail: Methods, status semantics, pagination, schema versioning, idempotency and rate limits.

concepts.title: FASTAPI
concepts.detail: Dependency injection, Pydantic models, async handlers and request lifecycle.

concepts.title: POSTGRESQL
concepts.detail: Keys, joins, transactions, isolation, indexes, EXPLAIN ANALYZE and migrations.

concepts.title: REDIS
concepts.detail: Cache-aside, TTL, cache stampede, invalidation and why it is not a source of truth.

concepts.title: AUTHENTICATION
concepts.detail: OIDC/session basics, authorization checks per resource, CSRF/XSS defenses.

stages.readiness: Build a multi-tenant project dashboard: React + TypeScript, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis optional, authenticated audit records.

lab.summary: Build a multi-tenant project dashboard: React + TypeScript, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis optional, authenticated audit records.
milestones: Define a versioned OpenAPI schema and generate a typed client. UI must render loading, empty, validation, outage and retry states.
Implement tenant-scoped SQL reads/writes and explicit ownership checks; never trust client-supplied tenant identifiers.
Create migrations with uniqueness constraints and rollback rehearsal. Measure queries with EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS).
Test browser-to-database flows; cover accessibility keyboard navigation and 401/403 distinctions.

failures.title: N+1 queries
failures.detail: List endpoint query count grows with returned records.

failures.title: Race
failures.detail: Concurrent edits silently overwrite changes without version guard.

failures.title: Caching
failures.detail: Wrong tenant data served due to incomplete cache key.

failures.title: Authz bypass
failures.detail: Resource ID guessed; backend trusts UI restrictions.

evidence: Verify cross-tenant reads/writes return 403 or 404 without data leakage.
Test transaction rollback under duplicate writes and simulated DB disconnect.
Use Playwright for one end-to-end path and EXPLAIN plans for slow queries.
adversarial: Can you prove data isolation in automated tests?
Where is the transaction boundary and why?
What happens when Redis is down?

stages.title: MATH + CLASSICAL ML
stages.subtitle: Linear algebra, probability, statistics and ML methodology

concepts.title: LINEAR ALGEBRA
concepts.detail: Vectors, dot products, matrix products, projections, SVD, norms and eigenspaces.

concepts.title: CALCULUS
concepts.detail: Gradients, Jacobians, chain rule, partial derivatives and optimization surfaces.

concepts.title: PROBABILITY
concepts.detail: Conditional probability, Bayes rule, distributions, expectation and variance.

concepts.title: STATISTICS
concepts.detail: Confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, bootstrap, power and multiple comparisons.

concepts.title: SUPERVISED ML
concepts.detail: Linear/logistic regression, trees, gradient boosting, regularization and bias-variance.

concepts.title: UNSUPERVISED
concepts.detail: Clustering, dimensionality reduction, anomaly detection and representation quality.

concepts.title: DATA LEAKAGE
concepts.detail: Feature construction, time-aware splits and target leakage detection.

concepts.title: METRICS
concepts.detail: F1 vs AUROC vs PR-AUC, calibration, operating point, business cost of mistakes.

stages.readiness: Build an interpretable fraud/abuse classifier using tabular data with time-based validation, calibration and threshold selection.

lab.summary: Build an interpretable fraud/abuse classifier using tabular data with time-based validation, calibration and threshold selection.
milestones: Write the data dictionary and event-time leakage policy before fitting; choose a naive baseline and log the class prevalence.
Use train/validation/test split chronologically. Keep preprocessing inside a fitted pipeline to prevent leakage.
Track PR-AUC plus recall at a fixed precision requirement; bootstrap intervals by user/session, not leaked rows.
Calibrate scores, choose decision threshold on validation only and report final untouched test metrics once.

failures.title: Label leakage
failures.detail: Predictor includes post-event status or chargeback field.

failures.title: Wrong metric
failures.detail: AUROC hides low precision in rare-positive data.

failures.title: Shift
failures.detail: Recent cohort distribution differs from historical training data.

failures.title: P-hacking
failures.detail: Repeatedly inspect and tune on test data.

evidence: Leakage audit: every feature timestamp <= prediction timestamp.
Report prevalence, PR-AUC, recall at precision target, and confidence interval.
Re-run with 5 seeds and show stability and worst cohort error.
adversarial: Why is the chosen split faithful to deployment?
What operational cost selects the threshold?
How much confidence does the sample size justify?

stages.title: DEEP LEARNING + TRANSFORMERS
stages.subtitle: Train, inspect and profile attention-based models

concepts.title: OPTIMIZATION
concepts.detail: SGD vs AdamW, learning-rate schedules, weight decay, gradient clipping and batch scaling.

concepts.title: PYTORCH
concepts.detail: Tensor shapes, autograd graph, dataloaders, inference_mode, checkpoint state.

concepts.title: NEURAL NETWORKS
concepts.detail: Activations, initialization, residuals, layer norm and gradients.

concepts.title: NLP
concepts.detail: Byte/wordpiece tokenizers, OOV, special tokens, sequence length and padding.

concepts.title: ATTENTION
concepts.detail: Q, K, V, masked softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V; causal vs bidirectional masks.

concepts.title: TRANSFORMERS
concepts.detail: Residual attention + MLP blocks, positional representations, KV cache at inference.

concepts.title: GPU FUNDAMENTALS
concepts.detail: Kernel launch, memory bandwidth, activation memory, batch size and mixed precision.

concepts.title: MODEL QUALITY
concepts.detail: Train/val loss, overfit checks, reproducibility and benchmark datasets.

stages.readiness: Build and train a tiny autoregressive transformer on a small text corpus; then profile inference with and without KV caching.

lab.summary: Build and train a tiny autoregressive transformer on a small text corpus; then profile inference with and without KV caching.
milestones: Implement a bigram baseline, then a transformer with causal attention and weight tying. Unit-test every tensor shape and mask.
Run a gradient-check on a tiny differentiable submodule; overfit one batch before full training.
Compare tokens/sec, GPU max allocated memory and train/validation perplexity across configurations.
Implement incremental decoding with KV cache; verify logits match full-prefill within a stated numerical tolerance.

failures.title: Future leakage
failures.detail: Attention mask permits model to see next tokens during training.

failures.title: NaN loss
failures.detail: Overflow in mixed precision or unstable normalization.

failures.title: Memory growth
failures.detail: Saved graphs accidentally retained across iterations.

failures.title: Wrong benchmark
failures.detail: Compare unequal context lengths or warm-up states.

evidence: Compare attention output to a trusted reference over small seeded tensors.
Assert future-token perturbations cannot affect earlier causal positions.
Profile eager attention vs optimized SDPA and explain speed/memory trade-offs.
adversarial: Derive attention tensor dimensions on paper.
Where does memory scale quadratically in sequence length?
How do KV caches alter memory and latency?

stages.title: GENAI + CONTEXT ENGINEERING
stages.subtitle: LLM inference, decoding, fine-tuning and context quality

concepts.title: LLM BASICS
concepts.detail: Tokenization, context limit, prefill vs decode, temperature, top-p and stop sequences.

concepts.title: MODEL SELECTION
concepts.detail: Quality/cost/latency/privacy trade-off, benchmark tasks and fallback policy.

concepts.title: INFERENCE
concepts.detail: KV cache, batch scheduling, quantization, throughput and context-length penalty.

concepts.title: PROMPTING
concepts.detail: Role hierarchy, system instructions, examples, negative constraints and task framing.

concepts.title: CONTEXT ENGINEERING
concepts.detail: Selection, deduplication, ordering, compression, source metadata and freshness.

concepts.title: FINE-TUNING
concepts.detail: SFT vs LoRA/PEFT vs full tuning; train when behavior/format is not solved by context.

concepts.title: MULTIMODAL
concepts.detail: Images, audio, speech, document parsing and alignment of evidence across modalities.

concepts.title: GROUNDING
concepts.detail: Provenance, uncertainty, citations, faithful synthesis and refusal when evidence absent.

stages.readiness: Ship a model router for text extraction and question answering, with explicit context budgets and a held-out task suite.

lab.summary: Ship a model router for text extraction and question answering, with explicit context budgets and a held-out task suite.
milestones: Create a task inventory and fixed evaluation set for extraction, classification, long context and multi-step reasoning.
Test three model configurations under identical prompts. Measure p50/p95 TTFT, completion time, output tokens and error rate.
Implement deterministic context budgeting: keep policies, select relevant evidence and reject overflow before request.
Explore LoRA only after documenting which failure types prompting/RAG cannot fix; protect against training contamination.

failures.title: Lost in the middle
failures.detail: Relevant passage buried in excessively long context.

failures.title: Prompt injection
failures.detail: Retrieved text masquerades as higher-priority instruction.

failures.title: Model drift
failures.detail: New model version silently changes output behavior.

failures.title: Spend explosion
failures.detail: Long context plus retries multiplies token costs.

evidence: Token counting uses the selected model tokenizer or a conservative bound.
Measure loss in answer quality after removing irrelevant context.
Compare router policy with a single-model baseline for cost and accuracy.
adversarial: When is retrieval better than fine-tuning?
Which tasks justify a larger model?
Why can a bigger context reduce answer quality?

stages.title: LLM APPLICATION ENGINEERING
stages.subtitle: Tool contracts, reliable async execution and cost controls

concepts.title: STRUCTURED OUTPUT
concepts.detail: Model schema enforcement plus local Pydantic validation and unknown-value handling.

concepts.title: TOOL CALLING
concepts.detail: Whitelist registry, typed arguments, authorization and explicit side-effect confirmation.

concepts.title: STREAMING
concepts.detail: Server-sent events / websockets, cancellation, partial responses and client disconnect.

concepts.title: ASYNC CONCURRENCY
concepts.detail: Semaphore limits, timeouts, cancellation propagation and connection pools.

concepts.title: RETRIES
concepts.detail: Only retry transient failures; exponential backoff, jitter, deadlines and idempotency.

concepts.title: ROUTING
concepts.detail: Model budgets, fallback paths, health checks and measured quality regression.

concepts.title: CACHING
concepts.detail: Cache deterministic public work; never mix tenant/private contexts.

concepts.title: RATE ECONOMICS
concepts.detail: Token reservations, per-tenant quotas, queue discipline and admission control.

stages.readiness: Implement a provider-agnostic typed extraction service that streams progress and enforces per-tenant dollar and token budgets.

lab.summary: Implement a provider-agnostic typed extraction service that streams progress and enforces per-tenant dollar and token budgets.
milestones: Define a Provider protocol and a strongly typed Extraction model. Normalize errors into timeout, throttled, invalid output and provider outage.
Bound concurrency with a semaphore; pass an absolute deadline and cancel upstream work on client disconnect.
Use input idempotency keys and a durable usage ledger. Reserve projected spend then reconcile actual provider usage.
Run contract tests using a fake transport and one live provider sandbox; verify schema failures do not bypass billing controls.

failures.title: Retry storm
failures.detail: Client and gateway both retry; effective QPS explodes.

failures.title: Partial streaming
failures.detail: Disconnected consumers leave model requests running.

failures.title: Output smuggling
failures.detail: Model produces valid JSON but unsafe or unauthorized action.

failures.title: Semantic cache
failures.detail: Similar query returns another tenant context.

evidence: pytest-asyncio: cancel 500 requests; no tasks or connections leak.
Hypothesis: malformed JSON, extra fields, empty strings and invalid numeric values.
Load: check error and cost metrics while quotas or provider rate limits trigger.
adversarial: What exactly is idempotent across retries?
Do your p95s include provider timeouts?
How is usage reconciled after interrupted streaming?

stages.title: RAG ENGINEERING
stages.subtitle: Treat retrieval and grounded generation as separate systems

concepts.title: INGESTION
concepts.detail: PDF/HTML/text parsing, tables, OCR confidence, de-duplication and document versions.

concepts.title: CHUNKING
concepts.detail: Semantic boundaries, overlap, parent-child structure, source offsets and token limits.

concepts.title: VECTOR SEARCH
concepts.detail: Embeddings, cosine/L2, exact vs ANN, HNSW tuning and recall trade-off.

concepts.title: LEXICAL SEARCH
concepts.detail: BM25/FTS for exact terms, identifiers, numbers and rare proper nouns.

concepts.title: HYBRID
concepts.detail: RRF or weighted fusion plus optional cross-encoder reranking on candidate pool.

concepts.title: FILTERING
concepts.detail: Tenant, ACL, time, tags; apply authorization before handing documents to model.

concepts.title: GENERATION
concepts.detail: Evidence packing, source IDs, attribution and evidence-insufficient responses.

concepts.title: ADVANCED RAG
concepts.detail: Query rewriting, multi-query, self-correction and graph retrieval only if eval wins.

stages.readiness: Create a tenant-safe policy/document Q&A system with corpus versioning, hybrid retrieval, citations and a no-answer behavior.

lab.summary: Create a tenant-safe policy/document Q&A system with corpus versioning, hybrid retrieval, citations and a no-answer behavior.
milestones: Ingest a corpus with known source spans; store checksum, tenant ID, document version, ACL and chunk offsets.
Baseline lexical and dense retrieval independently; then combine using RRF and rank by a measured reranker.
Build a labeled query set: answerable, missing evidence, conflicting passages, stale revisions, and adversarial injections.
Compute recall@k, nDCG@k, citation precision, groundedness and end-to-end time/cost. Tune one component at a time.

failures.title: Wrong evidence
failures.detail: High cosine similarity but wrong policy version.

failures.title: Injection
failures.detail: Document text instructs model to reveal secrets or call tools.

failures.title: Index regression
failures.detail: ANN index recall drops for filtered small subpopulations.

failures.title: Stale answer
failures.detail: Deleted or superseded pages persist in embeddings.

evidence: Gold queries split by category and time, not randomly duplicated paraphrases.
Verify each returned chunk passes permission and version checks.
Compare exact scan vs HNSW approximation recall; inspect filtered-query plans.
adversarial: Is retrieval quality separable from generation quality?
What happens if no credible evidence exists?
How do you prove every citation resolves to its source span?

stages.title: AI AGENTS + MCP
stages.subtitle: Actions, permissions, memory and tool boundaries

concepts.title: AGENT BOUNDARY
concepts.detail: A model proposes; a deterministic executor authorizes and performs tools.

concepts.title: TOOLS
concepts.detail: Typed JSON schemas, bounded arguments, allowlisted targets and safe error results.

concepts.title: MEMORY
concepts.detail: Working context vs persistent user preferences vs event log; explicit retention policies.

concepts.title: REASONING PATTERNS
concepts.detail: ReAct-style loops, planning, reflection and decomposition measured by task success.

concepts.title: MCP
concepts.detail: Client/server protocol, exposed tools/resources/prompts and trust boundary for remote servers.

concepts.title: SECURITY
concepts.detail: Scopes, least privilege, human approval and a sandbox for untrusted code or browsing.

concepts.title: STATE
concepts.detail: Versioned execution record; dedupe side effects with action IDs and idempotency.

concepts.title: ECONOMICS
concepts.detail: Max steps, tool cost, wall-clock deadline, tokens spent and termination policy.

stages.readiness: Build a read-only research agent first, then enable one narrowly scoped write tool behind explicit human approval.

lab.summary: Build a read-only research agent first, then enable one narrowly scoped write tool behind explicit human approval.
milestones: Define a closed set of tool names and Pydantic argument types. Reject unknown actions regardless of model output.
Separate agent-generated arguments from authenticated user identity. Bind permissions server-side.
Keep an append-only event log: proposal, approval, tool request, response hash, budget and final outcome.
Simulate malicious tool responses, unavailable MCP servers, repeated tool calls and approval expiration.

failures.title: Confused deputy
failures.detail: Tool uses server secrets on behalf of untrusted model output.

failures.title: Unbounded loop
failures.detail: Agent repeatedly searches without progress or budget checks.

failures.title: Memory leak
failures.detail: Stores secrets or personal data beyond retention policy.

failures.title: Supply chain
failures.detail: Third-party MCP server changes tools/scopes without review.

evidence: Prompt injection cannot grant scopes or bypass an approval check.
Repeated same action ID produces one external side effect.
Malformed MCP responses or resource updates do not crash orchestration.
adversarial: What authority is delegated to the model?
Can a tool return instructions that override the developer policy?
What is the rollback/compensation path after a write?

stages.title: AGENT ORCHESTRATION
stages.subtitle: State machines before framework abstractions

concepts.title: STATE MODEL
concepts.detail: Explicit finite-state machine with transition preconditions and invariants.

concepts.title: PERSISTENCE
concepts.detail: Save checkpoints and event history so a restart resumes with correct semantics.

concepts.title: WORKFLOWS
concepts.detail: Sequential, parallel, conditional and event-driven executions with join barriers.

concepts.title: ROUTING
concepts.detail: Select tool/model/agent based on policy, task state and confidence, not buzzwords.

concepts.title: MULTI-AGENT
concepts.detail: Supervisor-worker, handoff or collaboration only when specialization is measurable.

concepts.title: HUMAN-IN-LOOP
concepts.detail: Typed approval event, expiry, escalation, intervention and audit attribution.

concepts.title: COMPENSATION
concepts.detail: Sagas, idempotent replay and partial failure recovery for external side effects.

concepts.title: FRAMEWORK CHOICE
concepts.detail: Compare handwritten state machine with graph runtime on observability and reliability.

stages.readiness: Build a durable incident-triage workflow with research, classification, optional ticket creation and operator approval.

lab.summary: Build a durable incident-triage workflow with research, classification, optional ticket creation and operator approval.
milestones: Model workflow transitions in an enum; persist state version and causality IDs in a transactional store.
Add parallel read-only research branches and a deterministic merge rule; never race concurrent writers blindly.
Checkpoint before external side effects. Write idempotency keys and compensating actions where atomic commits are impossible.
Compare single-agent and multi-agent variants on held-out tasks; retain the simpler design unless improvement is material.

failures.title: Stale state
failures.detail: Node writes based on outdated version after parallel work.

failures.title: Infinite graph
failures.detail: Looping planner cannot meet termination condition.

failures.title: Bad handoff
failures.detail: Agent receives incomplete or overshared context.

failures.title: Framework opacity
failures.detail: Automatic retries silently duplicate a payment/ticket action.

evidence: Replay 10k event streams; end state must be deterministic.
Crash before/after tool commit and prove one externally visible action.
Test parallel join order, duplicate messages and stale operator approvals.
adversarial: Show the complete transition graph with illegal edges.
Why use multiple agents rather than one with tools?
Where are replay safety and exactly-once illusions broken?

stages.title: EVALUATION + OBSERVABILITY
stages.subtitle: Measure outputs, retrieval, actions and system behavior

concepts.title: LLM EVAL
concepts.detail: Task accuracy, relevance, hallucination, refusal, toxicity and calibrated judge rubrics.

concepts.title: RAG EVAL
concepts.detail: Retrieval recall/precision/nDCG, support evidence, citation accuracy and abstention.

concepts.title: AGENT EVAL
concepts.detail: Task success, tool choice, argument validity, trajectory safety and completion costs.

concepts.title: GOLDEN SETS
concepts.detail: Stratified, deduplicated, adjudicated examples with answer criteria and versioning.

concepts.title: STATISTICAL RIGOR
concepts.detail: Confidence intervals, paired bootstrap, sample size, multiple tests and selection bias.

concepts.title: TRACING
concepts.detail: Request > LLM call > retrieval > tool > DB spans, correlation IDs, redaction.

concepts.title: METRICS
concepts.detail: TTFT, end-to-end p50/p95/p99, tokens, spend, cache hit, errors, SLA burn rate.

concepts.title: EXPERIMENTATION
concepts.detail: Shadow tests, canary rollout, A/B design and predeclared stop conditions.

stages.readiness: Build an evaluation harness that rejects a new retrieval/model configuration if quality, safety or cost regresses.

lab.summary: Build an evaluation harness that rejects a new retrieval/model configuration if quality, safety or cost regresses.
milestones: Create gold cases spanning normal, adversarial, rare and high-impact slices. Each item stores expected assertions and provenance.
Record raw model outputs, retrieval IDs, prompts, configuration hash, token usage and deterministic evaluator versions.
Apply paired bootstrap or stratified confidence intervals to quality deltas. Report statistical uncertainty, not just a winner.
Instrument OpenTelemetry spans; aggregate by model, task, tenant and deployment version without logging secrets.

failures.title: Judge gaming
failures.detail: LLM-as-judge rewards verbosity rather than factual correctness.

failures.title: Missingness
failures.detail: Failed calls omitted from latency and outcome denominators.

failures.title: PII in traces
failures.detail: Raw inputs or retrieved private text leak into telemetry.

failures.title: A/B contamination
failures.detail: Same user receives mixed treatment or evaluation items enter training.

evidence: Run blind adjudication for at least 30 disputed cases.
Inject retrieval failures and tool permission denials; ensure trace spans expose root cause.
Regression gate uses predeclared threshold with CIs and slices, not cherry-picked score.
adversarial: What is your sampling unit: request, user or document?
How are scores audited for judge bias?
Which alert fires before customers report failure?

stages.title: SECURITY + GENAI OPS
stages.subtitle: Threat models, release gates and operations at scale

concepts.title: PROMPT INJECTION
concepts.detail: Direct, indirect, tool-output and retrieval-borne instructions crossing trust boundaries.

concepts.title: DATA SAFETY
concepts.detail: PII classification, retention, encryption, data egress controls and tenant isolation.

concepts.title: TOOL SECURITY
concepts.detail: Least privilege, scoped credentials, per-action approval and sandbox isolation.

concepts.title: SAFETY GATES
concepts.detail: Input and output policy checks; distinguish policy violations from model uncertainty.

concepts.title: SUPPLY CHAIN
concepts.detail: Dependency lockfiles, image signing, SCA, model weights provenance and SBOM.

concepts.title: REPRODUCIBILITY
concepts.detail: Dataset, prompt, model, embedding, chunker and evaluator version identifiers.

concepts.title: RELEASE ENGINEERING
concepts.detail: Immutable images, staged rollout, shadow traffic, canaries and rollback triggers.

concepts.title: INCIDENT RESPONSE
concepts.detail: Threat detection, log correlation, containment, root cause and blameless evidence.

stages.readiness: Hardening sprint: make an agentic document system resistant to injection, data exfiltration and release regressions.

lab.summary: Hardening sprint: make an agentic document system resistant to injection, data exfiltration and release regressions.
milestones: Write a threat model mapping assets, trust boundaries, attackers, entry points and impact; prioritize by likelihood x consequence.
Curate a red-team corpus with malicious PDFs, tool outputs, role spoofing, exfiltration requests and cross-tenant probes.
Add deterministic allow/deny rules around tools and validated output schemas; do not treat the LLM as the authorization layer.
Create CI/CD release policy: security tests, eval gate, canary, rollback and on-call runbook with secret rotation.

failures.title: SSRF / redirect
failures.detail: Domain allowlist bypass via DNS rebinding or redirects.

failures.title: Secret leakage
failures.detail: Prompt/model trace records credentials or sensitive docs.

failures.title: Release collision
failures.detail: Prompt and dataset versions changed without linked evaluation.

failures.title: Unsafe recovery
failures.detail: Rollback restores code but not incompatible DB schema or vector index.

evidence: Attempt 100+ role, tool and retrieved-document injection payloads.
Secret canary must never be exposed in model output, logs, traces or tools.
Canary rollback is rehearsed after simulated rise in groundedness errors.
adversarial: Can you enumerate all trust boundaries?
Are secrets ever visible to model-generated text?
What objective metric forces rollback?

stages.title: CLOUD + AI SYSTEM DESIGN
stages.subtitle: Architect reliable and economical end-to-end AI products

concepts.title: ARCHITECTURE
concepts.detail: Bounded contexts, API gateway, workers, data planes and control planes.

concepts.title: PROVIDER MAPPING
concepts.detail: AWS Bedrock / SageMaker; GCP Vertex AI / Cloud Run; Azure AI / AKS.

concepts.title: COMPUTE
concepts.detail: CPU vs GPU, throughput, cold starts, batching, reserved vs on-demand capacity.

concepts.title: STORAGE
concepts.detail: OLTP PostgreSQL, object storage, vector indexes, queues and event logs.

concepts.title: SCALABILITY
concepts.detail: Load shedding, queue length, autoscaling, tenant quotas and multi-region limits.

concepts.title: RELIABILITY
concepts.detail: SLOs, error budgets, timeouts, circuit breakers, replay and disaster recovery.

concepts.title: LATENCY
concepts.detail: Latency budget by hop, p99 tail amplification, prefill/decode and hot-path cache.

concepts.title: COST
concepts.detail: Token pricing, GPU utilization, vector index costs, observability overhead and unit economics.

stages.readiness: Design and ship the final production-style AI knowledge/workflow platform in one cloud with portable contracts.

lab.summary: Design and ship the final production-style AI knowledge/workflow platform in one cloud with portable contracts.
milestones: Write a one-page architecture decision record with product SLO, security classification, traffic forecast and economic constraints.
Derive QPS, concurrency, queue capacity, provider rate quota and cost per successful request; choose managed vs self-hosted inference.
Use infrastructure-as-code, private secrets and zero-downtime schema strategy; deploy a canary and alert on error-budget burn.
Run outage drills: provider 429, DB read-only, object-store slowdown, model drift, zone failure and corrupted index.

failures.title: Tail latency
failures.detail: One slow dependency amplifies p99 across fan-out.

failures.title: Noisy neighbor
failures.detail: Heavy tenant starves others without quotas and admission control.

failures.title: Regional outage
failures.detail: Data sovereignty/recovery assumptions are undocumented.

failures.title: Cost cliff
failures.detail: Autoscaling adds expensive GPU replicas at low utilization.

evidence: Report p50/p95/p99, error rate, backlog and cost under load at forecast and 2x traffic.
Show restore from backup and vector reindex against an explicit RTO/RPO.
Run security and load tests on deployed infrastructure, not only laptops.
adversarial: Draw a data flow and identify every trust boundary.
Can you bound worst-case spend during a retry storm?
What would make you change models or providers?

capstone.title: EvidenceOps AI platform
capstone.summary: authenticated teams upload policy and incident documents, ask evidenced questions, and request bounded follow-up actions. A grounded answer must cite source spans; writes require approval. The platform logs usage, versions data, and supports offline replay of evaluations.

exit: ≥ 85/100 in external code/design review, zero critical security defects, repeatable load and recovery drills, every claim reproducible from stored evidence.
